content.body:

and - `reviewerProvider` as the other member of the configured pair. - The latch is durable operational state and is loaded on crash/restart before any rotated dispatch. - Every ordinary and spike Engineer dispatch, Engineer retry, address-findings loopback, mechanical rebase follow-up, and Engineer rebase-brief dispatch uses the latched `engineerProvider`. - A later configuration change or rotation disable cannot switch either provider for a claimed card. - A board `Provider` value that differs from the latch routes the card to `Engine Review` as an explicit inconsistency before further agent work or merge. - A missing/unreadable latch for a claimed rotated card fails closed; it never recomputes from current config and never falls back to the default adapter. - Provider failure continues through DH-18 against the assigned adapter; there is no same-provider substitution. - Unrotated cards preserve the existing static per-role behavior and journal compatibility. - TDD: focused Node tests land first, then implementation. - `npm run test:harness` passes. ## Test-matrix row Add `NI-provider-rotation-latch` covering at least: - first lease claim atomically records the board-selected Engineer and opposite Reviewer pair; - restart and config-change recovery reuse the recorded pair; - ordinary/spike Engineer retries and both rebase paths stay on `engineerProvider`; - post-claim board mismatch and unreadable/missing rotated state fail closed; and - legacy unrotated journal records keep current behavior. ## Dependencies - Native `blocked_by`: #881 and #935 (ROT-1). ## Non-goals - Do not dispatch the Reviewer from the opposite provider yet. - Do not extend the review marker or merge gate yet; ROT-3 owns the complete merge-authority proof. - Do not enable live rotation yet. --- ## Preserved comment thread (3) from williacj/cowrite#936 _Carried verbatim; native threading and authorship dates do not survive recreation._
williacj — 2026-08-01 🚦 **Escalated to `Engine Review`** by the harness engine (H-5 escalation router, dev-harness §6, DH-29 two-stage). **Reason:** 3 rebase-loopback round(s) at head 1180e616 could not produce a mergeable branch — a human needs to resolve the conflict (§6). A bounded triage pass verifies this by execution and either resolves it or forwards it to `Needs CJ`. To resume once it lands there: resolve the decision above, then comment here and move this card back to **Ready**. The engine re-pulls a Ready card automatically (DH-1) — no engine restart needed.
williacj — 2026-08-01 🔍 **Triage pass (DH-29 two-stage, `.claude/agents/triage.md`)** — attempt 1 for this landing (0 prior `escalation_raised` events for #936 since its last `merge` event, per `node harness/data-reader.mjs telemetry --routing`). **Escalation reviewed:** category `unmergeable` — "3 rebase-loopback round(s) at head `1180e616` could not produce a mergeable branch — a human needs to resolve the conflict (§6)." **Verification by execution (clause 3), not re-reasoning from the escalation text:** 1. Telemetry trace for #936 (`rebase_round` events) shows round 1 and 2 went through the Engineer rebase-brief (`mechanical:false`), and round 3 succeeded via the engine's own cheap mechanical short-circuit (`mechanical:true`, `sha:09d7fe0009...`), landing head `1180e616`. The Reviewer then spent ~39 min (`02:37:31`→`03:16:10`) re-reviewing that head and returned **Sound**. 2. `origin/main`'s tip (`19f35b85`, PR #1021) landed at `2026-08-01T02:44:33Z` — **after** round 3's mechanical rebase (`02:37:30`) but **before** the merge attempt that triggered escalation (`~03:17:01`). `git merge-base 1180e616 origin/main` = `0363ada6`, one commit **behind** current `origin/main` tip — i.e. round 3's rebase was already stale by the time merge was retried, and `round = rebaseRound + 1 = 4 > MAX_REBASE_ROUNDS(3)` escalated immediately rather than attempting a 4th mechanical rebase. 3. In the card's own worktree, `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main` on `1180e616` **replays cleanly with zero conflicts** (`Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/feature/issue-936-...`) — the only diff introduced is main's own PR #1021 (windows-CI-classifier) content, nothing from this branch. I reset the local branch back to `1180e616` afterward (`git reset --hard 1180e616`, confirmed equal to `origin/`) — no state left mutated. 4. `gh pr view 1022 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` returned `MERGEABLE`/`UNSTABLE` a few minutes after the escalation, then `UNKNOWN`/`UNKNOWN` on a later poll — GitHub's own mergeability computation is flapping/eventually-consistent right now (consistent with `mergeable=CLEAN is not green`), so it's not a reliable signal either way; the git-level trial rebase above is the authoritative check. **Read (not verified further — informational):** `blocked_by` for #936 lists #935 and #881, both already `closed` — no missing/stale dependency edge here. **Assessment:** this reads as a timing artifact (main advanced during a long Reviewer round, staling round 3's rebase right as the engine's own bounded rebase-loopback budget (3) was exhausted), not a substantive content conflict — the branch demonstrably rebases clean onto current `main` right now. `unmergeable` isn't one of the categories Triage's hard scope (`.claude/agents/triage.md`) has a defined mechanical-resolution path for (unlike `provision-failed`/stranded-diff/verified-blocker/`blocked_by`), and re-queuing risks silently repeating the same bounded rebase-loopback that already exhausted itself once — that's CJ's call, not mine, per clause 5's "when in doubt, forward." **Forwarding to `Needs CJ` unresolved.** Given the verification above, resuming likely only requires moving this card back to `Ready` — the engine will re-pull it automatically (DH-1) and the next merge attempt should not need a 4th rebase round at all.
williacj — 2026-08-01 CJ resolution: the escalation was a spent rebase budget while main advanced. I rebased PR #1022 onto current main at 0c8a0122, resolved the matrix/runtime conflicts by retaining current-main contracts plus #936's latch behavior, and reran the harness and matrix gates green. Return to Ready for a fresh independent review at the new SHA.

content.title: ROT-3: Opposite-provider review and SHA-bound merge provenance
content.body:
> **Migrated from williacj/cowrite#937** (opened 2026-07-31).
> Moved 2026-08-03 as harness-product work under epic williacj/cowrite#173 (Rigger extraction).
> Recreated rather than transferred: GitHub forbids issue transfer from a private repo to a public one.
> Labels not carried (consumer-taste vocabulary per `setup-labels.mjs` HX-7 / spec §7.2.1, not engine contract): `type:feature`, `area:harness`, `conflict:harness-engine-tests`, `conflict:harness-run-loop`, `conflict:review-marker-contract`, `conflict:harness-provider-rotation`.
> Parent epic in cowrite was #650 — relink to its Rigger counterpart.

---

## Goal

Complete #650 by driving every Reviewer and re-review through the latched opposite provider, binding both providers into the exact-SHA review proof, enforcing that proof in the engine and server-side merge gate, and cutting Cowrite over only after the full path is fail-closed.

## Decision trace

- Parent epic: #650
- Ratified mechanism: DH-35 amendment, `docs/proposals/cross-provider-card-rotation.md`
- Builds on #935 (ROT-1)'s board/config contract and #936 (ROT-2)'s lease-bound provider-pair latch.
- Strengthens DH-8's coder≠reviewer and exact-SHA gates; it does not replace or loosen either.
- Extends DH-28's server-side merge enforcement.
- Requires the coordination-journal reliability fix in #881 / PR #904.

## Scope

- `harness/engine.mjs`
- Reviewer/spike-reviewer dispatch and publication prompts
- `.claude/hooks/review-marker.cjs`
- `.claude/hooks/review-gate.cjs`
- Focused engine and hook tests
- `harness/board-config.json` for the final atomic cutover
- `docs/test-matrix.md`

## Acceptance

- Every ordinary Reviewer, spike Reviewer, and re-review dispatch for a rotated card uses the journal's latched `reviewerProvider`, mechanically opposite `engineerProvider`.
- The exact PR head recorded in the journal is bound to that provider pair.
- A rotated card's SHA-bound marker carries `engineerProvider` and `reviewerProvider`.
- Both the engine and the server-side `gh pr merge` gate reject a rotated marker that:
  - omits either provider;
  - names equal providers;
  - disagrees with the journal's pair; or
  - is not bound to the exact current PR head.
- Legacy/non-rotated markers retain their existing schema behavior.
- Opposite providers never substitute for distinct dispatch identity; the existing coder≠reviewer gate remains independently enforced.
- Reviewer/provider failure waits or escalates through DH-18 against the assigned provider; no same-provider fallback can produce merge authority.
- Missing adapters, unreadable journal state, board/latch mismatch, and provenance mismatch all fail closed before merge.
- After the board field exists and the complete test suite is green, Cowrite's committed configuration enables `coordination.enabled: true` and `provider.rotation: ["claude", "codex"]` together. Startup validation succeeds on the resulting live configuration.
- Rollback remains one configuration change: disabling rotation affects only unclaimed cards, while claimed cards finish under their latch.
- TDD: focused Node and hook tests land first, then implementation.
- `npm run test:harness` passes.

## Test-matrix row

Add `NI-provider-rotation-review-gate` covering at least:

- ordinary/spike Reviewer and re-review dispatches use the latched opposite provider;
- rotated marker publication records both distinct providers for the exact SHA;
- engine classification rejects missing, equal, stale-SHA, or pair-mismatched provenance;
- the server-side merge gate independently rejects every malformed rotated proof;
- legacy marker fixtures retain current behavior;
- assigned-provider outage never falls back; and
- the committed Cowrite configuration validates with coordination and the `claude`/`codex` rotation enabled.

## Dependencies

- Native `blocked_by`: #881 and #936 (ROT-2).

## Non-goals

- Do not weaken Critical or recorded-decision escalation.
- Do not infer control state from telemetry.
- Do not add rotation to single-role senior/intake dispatches.

- `docs/proposals/harness-functional-spec.md` §4.1 (core roles — every consumer has these), §7.4 (agent file = identity, gates, procedure; engine prompt = situational context).

1. `templates/agents/engineer.md`, `templates/agents/reviewer.md`, and `templates/agents/planner.md` exist, derived from `.claude/agents/`, with project name, owner name, marker dir, escalation-lane display name (neutral default **`Needs Owner`**, per plan §8), verify commands, and constitution vocabulary replaced by #1070's placeholder convention.

5. #1070's render test covers all three files, and its `Test IDs` in `docs/test-matrix.md` are extended accordingly.
6. **Cowrite's own `.claude/agents/*.md` are unchanged.**

content.title: setup-board: guard the unguarded write and add --adopt recovery (not idempotence)
content.body:
**Execution Kind:** `change` (DH-45 §A) — ordinary implementation work, enters the Engineer pool.

## Goal

Make `setup-board.mjs` safe to re-run **without** making it idempotent, and add a recovery path for a lost `board-config.json`.

## The incident that motivates this

On 2026-08-03, provisioning Rigger's board ran `node harness/setup-board.mjs --owner williacj --title "Rigger"` from a cowrite checkout. The module derives its output path module-relatively, so it wrote its emitted config straight over **cowrite's live `harness/board-config.json`** — the address book for a different, populated, in-use board.

Nothing was lost only because the file had been backed up beforehand and was restored byte-identical (md5 `734b8833abbfd7a850aab852e74ed2c9`), and because the engine happened to be stopped, so nothing read the wrong config during the window. Neither of those was a property of the tool.

Two distinct defects are visible in that one run, and this card addresses the second:

1. **The write path is module-relative** — one of the nine location couplings recorded in **DH-42 §a**. Owned by the explicit-root refactor, *not* by this card.
2. **The write is unguarded** — the module overwrote an existing, valid config for a different board with no prompt, no diff, and no non-zero exit. That is this card.

## Why not idempotence

The obvious framing is "make it idempotent," and this card deliberately **rejects** that.

A GitHub Projects v2 board is not a file — it is a stateful external resource with work sitting on it. Idempotence means re-running converges the board to the declared schema, which forces a reconciler to answer questions with destructive answers: what if a Status option was renamed by hand? What if an option was deleted while items still reference it? What if a field exists with the right name and the wrong type? The failure mode of a naive reconciler is **deleting a column that has cards in it** — categorically worse than today's duplicate-board outcome, and it surfaces only on a board that already matters.

The module's `// Idempotency:` header comment should be updated to say this, rather than merely noting that the module is not idempotent.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Existing-config guard.** If a config file is already present at the resolved write path, exit **non-zero** without creating a project or writing anything, naming the existing file's `url` and `projectNumber` in the message. `--force` overrides.
2. **Duplicate-title guard.** If the owner already has a project with the requested title, exit non-zero naming its number and URL. `--force` overrides. (Distinct from AC1: a lost config file is exactly the case where AC1 cannot fire.)
3. **`--adopt <project-number>`.** Verify an existing project's fields and Status options against the schema this module would otherwise create, then emit `board-config.json` for it. **Creates nothing and mutates nothing.** On mismatch, exit non-zero naming every field/option that differs, in both directions (missing *and* unexpected). This is the recovery path for a lost address book, and the only reason full idempotence looked attractive.
4. **`--force` is loud** — prints exactly what it is about to overwrite or duplicate before doing it.
5. Tests cover each guard's fire and no-fire paths, `--adopt` agreeing and disagreeing, and the guards' interaction with `--force`. TDD: failing test first.
6. The module header's idempotency note is rewritten to state the reasoning above, not just the fact.

## Parked mechanism question — for the Architect, not for the Engineer to decide

**Does AC3's schema verification belong in `doctor.mjs` instead?**

**DH-42 §c** makes `doctor.mjs` the boundary validator, and "does this board's schema match what the engine expects" is a plain reading of that job. Implementing a second, independent schema-checker inside `setup-board.mjs` risks exactly the drift DH-42 §c exists to prevent — two checkers that agree on the day they are written and diverge afterwards.

Against that: `setup-board.mjs` is the module that *defines* the schema it creates, so the checker arguably belongs where the definition lives, with `doctor.mjs` calling into it rather than duplicating it.

Either shape is defensible; picking one is a mechanism call. **Do not guess — park and escalate if it is still open when this card is pulled.**

## Out of scope

- The module-relative write path (DH-42 §a, explicit-root refactor).
- Any change to what the board schema *is* — stages, fields, and options are untouched here.
- Full reconciliation of an existing board to the schema. Explicitly rejected above; a future card may revisit it with a non-destructive design, and should cite this rejection if so.

## Conflict domain

Declared in-body, per DH-45 §3.1 B: this repository provisions no `conflict:*` label vocabulary yet, and inventing one ad hoc — or defaulting to `conflict:none` because the vocabulary is missing — is forbidden. The merge surface is `setup-board.mjs` and its test file; it is disjoint from every other issue currently on this board.

## Provenance

Filed 2026-08-03 out of the incident above, during the cowrite→Rigger extraction (`williacj/cowrite#173`). Not migrated from a cowrite issue — this is new work, discovered by doing the extraction rather than planned by it.

content.title: Spike: is the Important severity bar calibrated, or absorbing findings that should be Minor?
content.body:
## Question (time-boxed)

**Of the `Needs Minor Revision` verdicts carrying exactly one Important, what fraction of those findings would a second, independent reviewer grade as Minor rather than Important?**

High → the severity bar, not engineer quality, is a material driver of the re-review loop, and the lever is recalibration. Low → the bar is right, and the remaining levers are prevention and round scope.

## Why ask

Across 857 verdict markers on 397 branches (2026-07-09 → 2026-08-05, measured from `.cowrite-review/*.json`):

- **Every** one of the 369 `Needs Minor Revision` verdicts carries `critical: 0` and `important >= 1`. There is not a single nit-only round.
- **230 of 369 (62%) carry exactly one Important.**

| crit / imp | count |
|---|---|
| 0 / 1 | 230 |
| 0 / 2 | 95 |
| 0 / 3 | 35 |
| 0 / 4+ | 9 |

Consistent with two very different stories:

1. **Calibrated** — reviews genuinely surface ~one real Important per round.
2. **Verdict-driven** — the gate reads *"any non-deferred Important ⇒ at most Needs Minor Revision"*, so a reviewer who believes a diff isn't quite ready reaches for one Important to say so. The count clusters at 1 because 1 is all the verdict requires.

The complete absence of `important: 0` non-Sound verdicts is what makes story 2 worth testing: severity and verdict are **mechanically coupled**, so counts alone cannot separate them.

This is a **measurement, not a change** — filed as a spike precisely because the honest answer might be "the bar is right, do nothing."

## Method

- Pre-register the sampling rule **before** inspecting outcomes (the cowrite#921 discipline).
- Sample single-Important `Needs Minor Revision` rounds from the window.
- An independent reviewer re-grades each finding against the code-review skill's severity rules, **blind to the original verdict**: Important / Minor / Deferred plus a one-line reason.
- Report disagreement rate with a confidence interval, broken down by lens (A1/A2/A4 dominate in a prior sample) and by whether the finding names an executable failure.
- Also record: was the original Important closed by a **code** change, or by a doc/comment/citation edit? A finding no commit can close is DH-33's `acceptAndMerge` channel — used on only **17 of 369** NM verdicts (4.6%). Under-use of an already-ratified escape hatch is a cheap finding if it shows up.

## Deliverable

Docs-only findings PR plus a journal verdict (DH-13, test-plan §9b). Spike code is throwaway, lives in gitignored `/spikes/`, never merges. Targets `williacj/cowrite` — the markers, telemetry, and review skill all still live there.

Recommend, do not apply: recalibration would be a code-review-skill change → DH-9 recorded-decision → CJ ratifies.

## Non-goals

- Re-grading any historical verdict or rewriting telemetry.
- Changing the verdict gate.
- Judging any individual reviewer dispatch.

content.title: harness: replace `gh project item-list` with a lean board CLI — it costs ~1 GraphQL point per board item
content.body:
## The problem

`gh project item-list` costs roughly **1 GraphQL point per board item**. The harness's own board query costs **2 points per 100-item page**. They return the same data.

Measured on 2026-08-05 against project 3 (426 items), each figure a before/after delta on `gh api rate_limit`:

| call | points |
|---|---|
| `harness/board.mjs` `buildItemsQuery`, one 100-item page | **2** |
| full 426-card board via `allCards()` (5 pages) | **10** |
| `gh project item-list --limit 300` | **304** |
| `gh project item-list --limit 2000` (426 items) | **506** |
| targeted single-issue project-status query | **1** |

So the CLI convenience costs ~50x the lean query for identical information. The GraphQL budget is 5,000 points/hour, which makes a single `item-list` call ~10% of the hour.

This is not theoretical: the budget was fully exhausted on 2026-08-05 and the engine logged `gh api graphql failed … API rate limit already exceeded`, retrying on backoff. The dominant consumers were exploratory `item-list` calls.

## Root cause — a gap in the CLI, not a bad habit

`harness/board.mjs`'s CLI (`:1023`) exposes:

```
add-card   <issueNodeId>
move       <itemId> <stage>
set-field  <itemId> <...>
ready                        ← Ready queue only
```

There is **no full-board dump**. `allCards()` is already exported (`harness/board.mjs:929`) and already used by the engine and by `harness/dashboard.mjs:356` (behind `makeBoardCache`), but it has no command-line surface. So anyone needing board state — a human, or an agent following a doc — has exactly one convenient option, and it is the 300–500 point one.

Nothing in the harness *code* calls `gh project item-list`. This is purely a docs-and-humans path.

## What to change

All paths below are in the **cowrite** repo (pre-extraction).

**1. Add a `cards` command to `harness/board.mjs`'s CLI.** Print `allCards()` as JSON, alongside the existing `ready`. Drop-in replacement for `gh project item-list --format json` at ~10 points instead of ~430.

**2. Add a `card <issue>` command in the same change.** The most common need is one card's column, not the whole board — and that is a 1-point targeted query rather than a 10-point full read. Shipping only `cards` leaves the cheapest case unserved and invites a full-board read for a single lookup.

**3. Replace the incantation in two docs:**
- `docs/proposals/re-planner-card-authority.md:17`
- `docs/proposals/parked-proposal-consolidation.md:9` and `:100`

Both instruct agents to verify board state with `gh project item-list 3 --owner williacj --limit 300 --format json` before citing figures — 304 points every time an agent obeys.

## What NOT to change

**Leave `docs/dev-harness.md` alone.** Its only mention is inside DH-31's evidence citation (*"a real `Needs CJ` depth of 12 (board truth, `gh project item-list 3`)"*) — a past-tense record of how a measurement was actually taken. Rewriting it would falsify the record. It is also DH-9's normative surface, so it would need ratification for no benefit.

## Testing

Harness layer only — `npm run test:harness` (no Rust, no frontend; suite-scoping per CLAUDE.md). TDD: the failing test comes first — a `board.mjs` CLI test asserting `cards` emits parseable JSON for a fixture board and `card <issue>` returns that issue's field values, both against the existing injected-`exec` seam the other CLI tests already use. No live `gh` in tests.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- `stageNames` are configurable (HX-11) — do not hardcode a `Status` literal in the new commands.
- `allCards()` carries the `#531`/`#558` short-read and `totalCount` completeness guards. Route the new command through it rather than re-issuing `buildItemsQuery` directly, so the CLI inherits the same fail-closed behavior.
- Worth considering as a follow-up, not in scope here: a deny rule for `gh project item-list` so the expensive path cannot be reached by reflex. The CLI gap is the cause; a deny rule is the belt.

content.title: harness throughput: run a controlled concurrency 3-to-4 experiment
content.body:
> **Migrated from williacj/cowrite#952** (opened 2026-07-31).

> **Cross-repo note:** its parent epic williacj/cowrite#953 deliberately REMAINS in cowrite; this child left. That epic loses this result.

---

## Purpose

Determine whether increasing the bounded coding pool from 3 to 4 raises delivered throughput after quality/routing work and the full #1008 contention-maintenance epic have succeeded. This is a separate controlled operation; it is not part of #1008's success bar.

## Preconditions

- The #913 quality follow-up and its selected interventions are complete.
- Execution-kind Ready admission is active for newly created cards.
- #1008 has closed through the telemetry-complete #1018 observation window.
- Conflict declarations and #951 scheduler enforcement are active.
- The serialized finalization lane is active and normal concurrency 3 met its acceptance thresholds.
- `maxEpicsInFlight` remains 2.

## Method

- Pre-register baseline and trial windows measured in engine-running hours, not calendar time.
- Hold provider mix, epic cap, priority policy, finalization cap, and review/merge gates constant.
- Change only coding concurrency from 3 to 4 for the trial.
- Use #1015's permanent report definitions and compare:
  - merges per engine-running hour;
  - synchronizations per merge and percent with more than one;
  - finalization queue wait/service time and utilization;
  - `rebase_round` per merge;
  - review rounds and one-round merge rate;
  - escalation and no-progress rates;
  - `conflict_domain_idle`/misses;
  - CI queue/cancellation time;
  - usage-wait time and cost where available.

## Keep/revert rule

- Keep concurrency 4 only if merges per engine-running hour improve by at least 10-15% without a material regression in synchronization, rebase, review, escalation, defect-escape, finalization queueing, CI, or usage-wait signals.
- Otherwise restore concurrency 3 and record which bottleneck absorbed the additional worker.
- Any double-finalizer, same-domain overlap, or incomplete required telemetry aborts and restores 3 immediately.
- Do not change `maxEpicsInFlight` or finalization concurrency during the experiment.

## Acceptance criteria

- The sampling rule, window boundaries, denominators, and thresholds are committed before trial outcomes are read.
- Start/end engine lifecycle evidence makes active hours auditable.
- The result records both throughput and quality/cost guardrails with raw-event provenance.
- Configuration ends at the evidence-backed value.
- No historical telemetry is rewritten and missing evidence cannot pass.

## Expected surfaces

- engine configuration within the allowed concurrency values
- #1015's committed report/dashboard surface
- GitHub operation evidence and the resulting fixed-window report

`conflict:global`

No `conflict:*` label is applied until provisioned.

content.title: Engineer pre-flight: mutate every new assertion (DH-9)
content.body:
## Scope

Add a fifth control to the Engineer's Compact Pre-flight check, and record the extension on the DH-9 row that owns the pre-flight mechanism.

**Deferred to post-extraction by CJ (2026-08-05)** — not to be worked in the Cowrite repo. Drafted as williacj/cowrite#1159 (closed unmerged); the exact diff is preserved on branch `docs/engineer-preflight-mutation-check` there if it's useful to port rather than rewrite.

Under DH-9 this is a recorded-decision change → CJ ratifies (DH-7, proposer≠ratifier).

## The control

> **Mutate every new assertion you are relying on.** For each test you added or changed, break the production line it claims to pin — invert the condition, drop the term, reverse the sort, remove the call — and re-run just that test. A mutation the test still passes through means the test does not pin the behavior, and the row you added to `docs/test-matrix.md` is claiming coverage you do not have: fix the assertion, then restore the production line. Report which mutations you ran and that each was caught.

Self-check only. No new authority, no marker, no merge rights. Coder≠reviewer, the SHA-bound marker, and the independent Reviewer gate are untouched (DH-8). Like the original pre-flight it lands on the Engineer prompt and mints no standalone DH-#.

## Why — two premises moved

**1. The narrowing's justification expired.** DH-9 records that the pre-flight was narrowed (cowrite#785) because an **Opus-5** Engineer "self-verifies without" the retired scaffolding. `board-config.json` now sets `provider.roles.engineer = codex` — and cowrite#913's ratified, immutable baseline measured Codex rework at **2.333 vs Claude's 1.533**, ratio 1.52 against the ratified `<= 1.2` target, recorded FAIL. The stated reason no longer applies to the Engineer that actually runs.

**2. The rework signal did not hold.** Measured over 857 verdict markers on 397 branches (2026-07-09 → 2026-08-05, from `.cowrite-review/*.json` — note `harness-metrics.jsonl` lags):

| | rounds | share |
|---|---|---|
| First reviews (unavoidable) | 397 | 46% |
| Findings-driven re-reviews (NM 369 + RSC 32) | 401 | 47% |
| Sound-after-Sound (pure SHA tax — see #21/#22) | 64 | 7.5% |

One-round merge rate **43% overall, 32% for branches first reviewed on/after 07-30**, against the ratified `>= 55%` target. It regressed.

## Why this control specifically

All 369 `Needs Minor Revision` verdicts carry `critical: 0` and `important >= 1`; **230 carry exactly one Important.** The loop is one-Important rounds — "reduce nits" is not an available lever (whether the bar itself is calibrated is #23).

Sampling those Importants by lens, **A4 (test discipline) ties A1 for the largest share**, and its dominant shape is an assertion that passes without exercising the behavior its `docs/test-matrix.md` row claims: an unwired seam, a class/text existence check standing in for the real property, a malformed escape rendering the assertion vacuous.

The Reviewer already catches these by running mutations by hand. From a real round-2 report: *"I ran 8 mutations of the new code and all 8 were caught, including the two that round 1 showed survived."* This moves the same mechanical check one round earlier, to where the context is already loaded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The control lands on the Engineer prompt.
- [ ] The DH-9 row records the extension, the expired Opus-5 premise, and the measured baseline above.
- [ ] Required baseline/final suites unchanged; DH-8 gates unchanged.
- [ ] Post-change `review_round` telemetry is re-measured against the 43%/32% baseline before any claim of effect — and reported as correlational, since provider and other harness changes confound it (the cowrite#785 write-up's own standard).

## Context

Parent: **#3** (reduce Engineer rework). Related: **#21**/**#22** (DH-47 carry-forward), **#23** (severity calibration).

**Execution kind:** change · **Tier:** Opus · **High-Risk:** No · **Conflict domain:** harness-prompts

content.title: Epic: Completion contracts and final acceptance review for epics
content.body:
> **Migrated from williacj/cowrite#941** (opened 2026-07-31).
> Moved 2026-08-03 as harness-product work under epic williacj/cowrite#173 (Rigger extraction).
> Recreated rather than transferred: GitHub forbids issue transfer from a private repo to a public one.
> Labels not carried (consumer-taste vocabulary per `setup-labels.mjs` HX-7 / spec §7.2.1, not engine contract): `type:feature`, `area:harness`.

---

## Owner direction

CJ approved this plan on 2026-07-30. Epic completion must become an independently reviewed outcome, not an inference from every known child issue being closed. The same completion dimensions must enter during epic intake so decomposition does not omit the operational and cross-cutting work that recent manual closure analyses repeatedly found.

This is a feature-intake epic, not an executable implementation card. It must pass through the existing PM and Architect intake gates before decomposition.

## Problem

DH-19/DH-20 stop epic intake at `intake:carded` and say the open umbrella closes when its children merge, but there is no epic-level acceptance review or durable closure verdict. Closed children prove only that planned cards shipped. They do not prove that the original epic promise was fully decomposed, production-wired, documented, observable, or accepted end to end.

Recent closure analyses exposed the repeated failure mode:

- #172 required #831-#833 and then #857-#858 after green card suites still missed production configuration consumers, a canonical contract conflict, and integrated non-default acceptance coverage.
- #232 required a closure tranche #859-#861 for missing PR-opened telemetry, the operator runbook, deployment configuration, and live Slack acceptance.
- #603 required #646 and #906-#908 for missing production dispatch wiring, an unresolved completion bar, incorrect provider telemetry attribution, and stale documentation/decision status. The epic was also closed before its finalizer PR merged.

## Goal

Add one lifecycle spanning both ends of an epic:

1. **Intake completion contract:** PM-led intake records what proof the epic will owe across functional outcome, production wiring, documentation, telemetry, automated coverage, end-to-end/live acceptance, recovery, platforms/external services, deployment/configuration/secrets, decision reconciliation, and residual risk/deferrals. Every dimension is Required, N/A with rationale, or Deferred by explicit CJ disposition. Decomposition maps each required dimension to a card or named final acceptance activity.
2. **Independent final acceptance reviewer:** after the Re-planner finds no next tranche and no descendant work remains open or in flight, a distinct epic-review role reconstructs the original promise from ratified artifacts, audits current `main` and real production entry points, executes the applicable proof, looks for missing work beyond the planned child set, and publishes a durable verdict before closure.

## Required final-review coverage

The final reviewer must verify, as applicable:

- Ratified requirements, UX, architecture, and the original epic outcome are delivered.
- The capability is reachable through its real production entry point; injected helpers or isolated adapters alone are insufficient.
- Documentation and operator workflows match the shipped system and do not rely on facts hidden in child PRs/comments.
- Telemetry is complete end to end: authoritative emission, schema, attribution, persistence/dedup/recovery, downstream projection/reporting, documentation, and tests.
- Applicable unit, integration, test-matrix, platform, and end-to-end suites pass. Green tests must exercise the production composition and be non-vacuous.
- External integrations receive safe live acceptance when central to the outcome; unavailable surfaces are named as exceptions and never counted as passing evidence.
- Configuration, deployment, migration, secrets, failure/restart/recovery behavior, decision status, accepted risks, and explicit deferrals are reconciled.

## Verdict and routing contract

- **Complete:** publish the evidence-backed epic verdict, mark the epic accepted, then close it.
- **Incomplete:** keep the epic open and route concrete child cards for gaps already authorized by ratified artifacts; review again after they merge.
- **Decision required:** park the epic in `Needs CJ`; never silently narrow the completion contract.
- **Blocked:** keep the epic open with the blocker recorded.

The verdict must identify the reviewed `main` SHA, relevant specification state, descendant set, executed proof, and unexecuted surfaces. New or reopened descendants, or a changed completion contract, invalidate it. No closure summary may claim unmerged finalizer work as delivered.

## Mechanism requirements for intake design

- This must be a mechanically required epic-closure gate, not reviewer-memory prose alone.
- The closure state must remain reconstructable from durable board/GitHub facts; no hidden engine memory.
- The final reviewer is independent of epic authorship and is not the PR-oriented code-review lane.
- The reviewer writes no production code and does not self-ratify recorded-decision changes.
- The design must specify how out-of-band closure of a `type:epic` without a valid acceptance verdict is surfaced or corrected.
- Amend DH-19/DH-20 or add successor DH requirements/mechanism through the normal proposer-not-ratifier intake gates.
- Add telemetry and tests for dispatch, verdict routing, invalidation, retry/recovery, premature-closure defense, and no-op behavior for epics that are not closure candidates.

## Explicit non-goals

- Replacing per-card independent code review.
- Treating a closed child set as sufficient evidence.
- Requiring every possible suite or live mutation for every epic regardless of scope; intake classifies applicability and the final reviewer records what was and was not executed.
- Allowing the final reviewer to invent or ratify new product scope.

content.title: harness: design an auto-sweep out of the Blocked column — an unblocked Blocked card is currently indistinguishable from Needs CJ
content.body:
> **Migrated from williacj/cowrite#656** (opened 2026-07-26).
> Moved 2026-08-03 as harness-product work under epic williacj/cowrite#173 (Rigger extraction).
> Recreated rather than transferred: GitHub forbids issue transfer from a private repo to a public one.
> Labels not carried (consumer-taste vocabulary per `setup-labels.mjs` HX-7 / spec §7.2.1, not engine contract): `area:harness`.

---

## The problem

A card sitting in the **Blocked** column with **all native `blocked_by` edges closed and no `blocked:<reason>` label** is stuck: nothing in the harness moves it back to Backlog. `planner.mjs` (issue #321, `planner.mjs:338-369`) *detects* exactly this case and emits a `blocked_card_unlabeled` telemetry row, but **deliberately never auto-moves or auto-labels it** — the recorded rationale is that the planner cannot tell "genuinely done being blocked" from "someone forgot the `blocked:<reason>` label," so it leaves the disposition to a human/Re-planner.

The consequence (raised by CJ, 2026-07-25): an unblocked-but-still-`Blocked` card requires a human hand to advance — which makes the Blocked column **functionally identical to `Needs CJ`** for that card. That defeats the point of a distinct Blocked column. Live example: #416 sat in Blocked with both blockers (#415, #410) closed and no label; it only moved because a human noticed. It had been silently flagging `blocked_card_unlabeled` on every planner pass with nobody watching the telemetry.

## The design question

Define a rule under which a card may be **automatically promoted Blocked → Backlog** (or otherwise advanced) without a human. Candidate signal: *all `blocked_by` edges closed AND no `blocked:<reason>` label AND the card's own issue still open*. The design must resolve:

- **The #321 ambiguity head-on:** is "no label + no open blocker" safe to auto-promote, or does the label-forgotten risk mean the invariant should instead be "a Blocked card MUST carry a `blocked:<reason>` label" — enforced at the move-into-Blocked site — so that a label-less Blocked card is a provable defect, not an ambiguous state? (The `blocked:external` cards #445/#480 are correctly labeled and must be untouched by any sweep.)
- **Where the sweep lives** (planner replenish vs. the #217 closed-issue sweep vs. a new edge) and its interaction with the `blocked_card_unlabeled` telemetry it would replace or complement.
- **Failure direction:** fail-closed (leave in Blocked, keep flagging) must remain the safe default on any doubt or transient REST error, matching #321's existing fail-open-diagnostic discipline.

## Deliverable

A design proposal (recorded-decision delta touching the DH-9 harness-process surface, e.g. planner/board mechanics + any Blocked-column invariant). **Proposal only** — parks in `Needs CJ` for CJ ratification (proposer ≠ ratifier, DH-7). No mechanism is implemented on this card; it decomposes into implementation card(s) once ratified.

Refs: #321 (blocked-reason machine-readability + the detector this would build on), #416 (the live stale-Blocked incident), #445/#480 (`blocked:external` — must stay parked).

content.title: harness: engine should run as a polling daemon, not drain-and-exit — eliminate the drain-edge race that strands work
content.body:
> **Migrated from williacj/cowrite#673** (opened 2026-07-26).
> Moved 2026-08-03 as harness-product work under epic williacj/cowrite#173 (Rigger extraction).
> Recreated rather than transferred: GitHub forbids issue transfer from a private repo to a public one.
> Labels not carried (consumer-taste vocabulary per `setup-labels.mjs` HX-7 / spec §7.2.1, not engine contract): `area:harness`.

---

## Motivation

The engine currently **drains and exits** when a scheduling pass finds no Ready/in-flight/promotable cards. This races with the backlog-refill that happens at the same drain edge: on the 2026-07-25 overnight run, the re-planner batch-added 6 unblocked cards (#431, #569, #596, #614, #638, #651) to Backlog at 06:54 — *after* the final planner pass — and the engine exited without re-scanning them. They sat stranded until a manual `/start-engine`. The engine log never referenced them; `allCards` paginates correctly and fails closed, so this was **not** a board-read/truncation bug (#370/#531 class) — it is a **lifecycle race**: drain-detection and backlog-refill both fire at the drain edge and drain-then-exit wins.

Same theme as #656 (Blocked-column auto-sweep): "the board changed and nothing re-evaluated."

## Proposed direction (CJ, 2026-07-26)

Simplify the mental model: **the engine is a long-running daemon, not a batch job.** It never exits on an empty board — it polls for new work on an interval and only stops on a forced exit (or a bug). CJ-approved interval target: **poll every ~5 minutes** on an idle board (rate-limit-safe: ~200 REST/GraphQL requests per hour against the 5,000/hour authenticated budget; even 1-minute polling stays under ~1k/hr).

## Design requirements (all five ratified with CJ)

1. **Idle backoff, not busy-spin** — poll on an interval (~5 min baseline) that backs off when idle; never hammer the GitHub API.
2. **Continuous staleness gate** — the #425 stale-checkout gate runs *once at startup* today; a never-exiting daemon could run merged-away `harness/**` / `.claude/**` code indefinitely. The loop MUST periodically re-check "am I behind origin/main on the harness surface?" and pause/self-restart when it is. (Highest-risk new requirement.)
3. **Clean forced-exit contract** — a deterministic stop via sentinel file or signal; reuse the Slack pause/resume sentinel pattern (#275).
4. **Reconcile with existing run modes** — the daemon should subsume, not sit beside, #230 (supervised overnight) and #278 (Windows hosting); do not create a third lifecycle.
5. **Quiet telemetry when idle** — keep events transition-shaped (#127/#321 discipline) so an idle poll loop does not flood `harness-metrics.jsonl`.

## Scope / deliverables

Run the **full intake ladder** (PM requirements delta → Architect mechanism delta, each reviewed and CJ-ratified — full review, per CJ). Likely a new/changed **DH-#** governing engine lifecycle, plus the poll-loop mechanism, the continuous staleness re-check, and the forced-exit contract. Proposal only at each stage — parks in `Needs CJ` for ratification (DH-7, proposer ≠ ratifier). Decomposes into implementation cards once the design is ratified.

Refs: #656 (Blocked auto-sweep — sibling "nothing re-evaluated" gap), #425 (startup stale gate this must make continuous), #230/#278 (existing run modes to subsume), #275 (sentinel pattern), #127/#321 (drain/telemetry discipline). Incident: overnight run 2026-07-25→26, cards #431/#569/#596/#614/#638/#651.

content.title: PROPOSAL: make the scheduler pool knobs adjustable live — concurrency is the only control input that requires a full restart
content.body:
> **Migrated from williacj/cowrite#1064** (opened 2026-08-01).
> Moved 2026-08-03 as harness-product work under epic williacj/cowrite#173 (Rigger extraction).
> Recreated rather than transferred: GitHub forbids issue transfer from a private repo to a public one.
> Labels not carried (consumer-taste vocabulary per `setup-labels.mjs` HX-7 / spec §7.2.1, not engine contract): `type:feature`, `area:harness`, `conflict:harness-engine-tests`, `conflict:harness-operations`, `conflict:harness-run-loop`, `conflict:harness-scheduler`, `conflict:harness-telemetry`.

---

## Status: PROPOSAL — parks in `Needs CJ`

This adds a control input to the scheduler, extending DH-22's sentinel pattern, so CJ ratifies before code lands (DH-7/DH-9, proposer ≠ ratifier). Once ratified, implementation routes to the engine for independent review.

## Problem

Concurrency is resolved **once at startup** and can never be changed while the engine runs. Adjusting it requires a full service reload, which interrupts every in-flight worker.

`runCli` resolves it a single time (`harness/runtime.mjs:361-366`):

```js
const concurrency = argv.includes('--once') ? { n: 1, source: '--once' }
  : resolveConcurrency({
      cli: optionValue(argv, '--concurrency'),
      env: env.HARNESS_CONCURRENCY,
      config: config.concurrency,
    });
```

and hands the number down as a fixed parameter (`harness/engine.mjs:5461-5467`):

```js
export async function runConcurrentlyUntilDrained({
  deps, n = 1, maxTriageInFlight = ..., noMerge = false, log = () => {}, maxEpicsInFlight = ...,
})
```

Nothing re-reads the env var, `board-config.json`, or any control file on subsequent passes.

**All three pool knobs share this**, resolved together in `runCli`: `resolveConcurrency` (:363), `resolveMaxTriageInFlight` (:461), `resolveMaxEpics` (:467). So the gap is a family, not a single value.

## Why this is inconsistent with the engine's own design

The run loop already re-checks other control inputs on **every pass**:

- the pause sentinel `harness/engine-paused` (`engine.mjs:1111-1115`)
- the shutdown sentinel `harness/engine-shutdown-requested` (`runtime.mjs:34`)
- the keep-awake hold, deliberately re-asked each pass rather than latched, precisely so an out-of-band death is recovered (`engine.mjs:5469-5473`)

DH-22 established the rationale directly: the pause sentinel "is a control input, like `--concurrency` or the Priority field — durable is in fact *more* crash-correct than in-memory, since a respawn mid-pause stays paused." That reasoning names `--concurrency` as a peer control input, yet concurrency is the one that cannot be actuated live.

Board Priority — the other named peer — is likewise re-read every pass.

## Motivating observation (2026-08-01)

With `HARNESS_CONCURRENCY=4`, rebase contention grew measurably as workers collided on `main`:

- 3-hour window: **5 rebase rounds / 5 merges**
- 6-hour window: **13 rebase rounds / 6 merges** — over two rebases per merge

Each conflict dispatches an Engineer with a rebase brief instead of new work, so the 4th worker is plausibly costing more than it produces. Testing that hypothesis today means reloading the service and interrupting four in-flight workers — expensive enough that the experiment does not get run, and the knob stays mis-set.

This is the concrete cost: **a tuning knob that cannot be tuned without disruption does not get tuned.**

## Proposed change

Re-read the pool knobs on each scheduling pass, from a durable control input, following the shutdown sentinel's shape (a small JSON envelope with `schema_version`, since these carry values rather than mere presence).

**Reduction must be graceful — this is the critical semantic.** Lowering concurrency must NOT kill in-flight workers. The pool simply stops refilling freed slots until `inFlight < newN`, draining down naturally — exactly how DH-22's pause already behaves and how DH-34's `activeEpics` spill already works. Raising the value fills on the next pass.

Precedence should remain as documented (CLI > env > config), with the new control input taking effect over the startup-resolved value while present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Failing test first: with the engine running at N=4, actuating N=3 causes the pool to stop refilling until in-flight drops to 3, with no worker interrupted.
- [ ] Raising N fills the new slots on the next scheduling pass.
- [ ] In-flight cards are never abandoned, cancelled, or re-queued by a concurrency change.
- [ ] The same mechanism covers `maxTriageInFlight` and `maxEpicsInFlight`, or the card explicitly states why it does not.
- [ ] A change is recorded in telemetry (old value, new value, source) so a tuning experiment is auditable against throughput.
- [ ] An absent or malformed control input leaves the startup-resolved value untouched — never a silent reset to the default.
- [ ] A restart re-reads the control input, so a live change survives a respawn (the DH-22 crash-correctness argument).
- [ ] `docs/dev-harness.md` records the decision; the "resolved once at startup" reading is what changes.
- [ ] Tests join `docs/test-matrix.md`.

## Notes

- Scope is the *pool* knobs only. Not proposed for anything whose mid-run change would corrupt in-flight state.
- Should compose with, not duplicate, DH-34's epic WIP cap — both withhold slots, and they must not fight over the same idle worker.
- Related: DH-22 (pause sentinel as a durable control input, and its explicit `--concurrency` comparison), DH-34/#596 (epic WIP cap and auto-spill), #813 (shutdown sentinel envelope shape — the precedent for a value-carrying control file), #169 (board Priority as a live-read control input).

## Outcome

Rigger provides a work-centric Slack surface for continuous engine visibility, multi-turn read-only specialist conversation, explicit revision-bound decisions, reliable delivery and catch-up, and opinionated Steward recommendations. GitHub and governed artifacts remain authoritative.

This is the successor to Cowrite epic williacj/cowrite#232. The ratified DH-21/DH-22 amendment was landed by williacj/cowrite#1106 at Cowrite merge commit b350829a3f1a5b571e17a541429c7dfd217513d1 and remains historical and consumer-binding evidence in Cowrite.

Cowrite receives only a later adoption card after a Rigger release: pin the exact package version, provide project configuration and secrets, and record live acceptance. Do not create duplicate implementation cards in Cowrite or reopen #232.

This epic is intentionally not executable yet. When the Rigger board schema and intake labels exist, stamp it:

- type:epic
- area:harness

- the operator-selected Priority

The Architect gate comes before Planner decomposition. The architecture proposal must be authored against the ratified Cowrite amendment and then explicitly ratified before any implementation card reaches Ready.

- [ ] Rigger has stable repoRoot/stateDir, package/module boundaries, configuration loading, provider contracts, and test commands against which an architecture can be written.
- [ ] Rigger board fields, intake labels, conflict-domain vocabulary, and engine self-hosting are provisioned.
- [ ] The ratified amendment in williacj/cowrite#1106 is adopted into the Rigger requirements record without changing its intent.

Replace these checklist blockers with exact native blocked_by edges when the corresponding Rigger bootstrap issues exist.

## Ratified delivery order

1. Architect mechanism, schemas, module boundaries, migration, and conflict-domain map.
2. Durable conversation/event ledger and reliable outbound outbox foundation.
3. Work-detail, engine-detail, and eight-hour summary projections with per-user catch-up.
4. Triaged human attention and read-only multi-turn specialist conversation.
5. Revision-bound proposals, explicit confirmation, authoritative recording, and tracked-work resume.
6. Steward recommendations, outage/restart hard-path verification, staged rollout, and Phase 1 operating feedback.

These are dependency-ordered tranches, not six epics and not necessarily six issues. Planner should emit only the first executable tranche after architecture ratification; later tranches are extended at phase boundaries.

## Architecture constraints

- Preserve Slack as an optional sibling: Slack failure never blocks engine correctness, scheduling, review, or merge.
- Preserve existing governance and review-marker boundaries; conversational prose is never an implicit actuator.
- Use one Cowrite app identity initially, with configurable work-detail, engine-detail, and summary channels.

- Establish separate modules and precise conflict domains for transport, context, delivery, projections, summaries, conversation, and decisions.
- Use native blocked_by only for correctness dependencies and conflict domains only for predicted merge/rebase overlap.

Phase 1 is decision-bound control over already tracked work. General work creation, broad reprioritization, and a larger Slack control surface belong to a separately ratified Phase 2 epic after operating feedback.

content.title: DH-47: ratify rebase-only review carry-forward
content.body:
## Disposition requested

Ratify, amend, or decline the rebase-only review carry-forward proposal.

**Proposal doc + PR live in the Cowrite repo** (the harness code and constitution have not been extracted to Rigger yet): `docs/proposals/rebase-only-review-carry-forward.md`, landed by **williacj/cowrite#1161**.

This **loosens a DH-8 authorship clause**, so per that row's own requirement it needs CJ's ratification plus a decision-log entry on DH-8. Per the DH-46 / cowrite#1023 precedent, the DH-47 row is written into `docs/dev-harness.md` on disposition — not by the proposal PR.

## The actual question

Carry a `Sound` verdict onto a new head when the reviewed **content** provably did not change — a rebase, or a doc fix elsewhere in the tree.

Two mechanisms were considered:

- **Option A** — the engine assembles a mechanical proof; the **Reviewer** still writes the marker from a bounded brief.
- **Option B** — the engine writes the carried marker itself once the proof holds.

The proposal as filed recommends A on DH-8 grounds. **CJ challenged that framing on 2026-08-05 and the challenge holds:** for a *mechanical identity claim* (not a judgment), putting an LLM in charge of confirming deterministic git output is weaker than tested code, not stronger — an agent handed "this is rebase-only, confirm" confirms essentially every time. Option A's Reviewer dispatch is largely ceremony.

The genuinely non-ceremonial argument for A is **erosion resistance**: "the engine never writes a marker" is checkable at a glance; a four-condition gate needs re-auditing forever, and the pressure to widen it ("docs-only is obviously safe too") is relentless. cowrite#327's five successive merge-gate bypass rounds are this repo's own evidence that conditional gates erode here — but note that incident was resolved by making the gate *more mechanical* (DH-28's `reference-transaction` hook), not more judgmental, which cuts toward B.

## The real risk is the proof, and the filed proof was broken

`git patch-id` **strips whitespace**. Demonstrated:

```
def f():                 def f():
        return 1               return 1      ← 8-space vs 2-space Python indent
patch-id: f29971ed...    f29971ed...         ← IDENTICAL
```

Semantically different Python, same patch-id. The originally-filed check 1 would have carried a `Sound` verdict onto changed code wherever whitespace is load-bearing (Python, YAML, Makefiles). **No signature scheme catches this** — a Reviewer told "patch-ids match" signs off just the same.

Corrected proof — per-path **blob-hash** equality:

```
git rev-parse <reviewed-head>:<path>   vs   git rev-parse <new-head>:<path>
8-space blob: cb06ad1d...   2-space blob: be697ce9...   → differ, carry refused
```

Exact content hashes, no normalization, trivially unit-testable. Also catches commits silently dropped during rebase, which a patch-id multiset comparison can miss.

## Evidence for doing it at all

- 64 of 857 verdict markers (7.5%), across 50 branches, are Sound-after-Sound re-reviews returning no findings.
- cowrite#1157: six rounds, of which 3–6 were all `Sound` (a rebase and a doc correction each cost a full re-review).
- cowrite#1079's Reviewer already did the determination by hand: *"the seven rebased commits are patch-identical to the reviewed series."*
- Direct cost ~6 reviewer-hours. **The larger cost is the DH-46 interaction**: a rebase-driven re-review runs inside the serialized finalization fence, widening the window for a peer merge to stale the head again — the loop behind cowrite#1157's rounds 4–6.

## What CJ is actually deciding

1. **Option A or B** — ceremony vs. bright line, on the reasoning above.
2. Whether narrowing *the evidence a Reviewer may reach `Sound` from*, when content is provably identical to content already judged `Sound`, counts as "weakening a gate." If it reads as weakening, decline — it is not worth the invariant.

## Conflict domains

content.title: carry a Sound verdict across a rebase-only head move (DH-47)
content.body:
## Blocked until DH-47 is dispositioned

Do not start until **#21** is dispositioned. The mechanism (Option A vs Option B) and the exact proof are both decided there — this card implements whichever CJ ratifies. If declined, this closes with it.

**Code lives in the Cowrite repo** (`harness/engine.mjs`, `.claude/hooks/review-marker.cjs`) until extraction lands, so the implementation PR targets `williacj/cowrite`.

## Scope

When a branch's head moves but its reviewed **content** provably did not, skip the full-lens re-review.

`evaluateMarker` (`.claude/hooks/review-marker.cjs`) and both gates — the PreToolUse advisory and the `reference-transaction` hook — are **unchanged byte-for-byte**. Every merge still requires a marker for the exact head. What changes is only how that head's marker comes to exist.

## Proof — all must pass

1. **Content identity, by blob hash.** For every path the branch touches, `git rev-parse <reviewed-head>:<path>` == `git rev-parse <new-head>:<path>`, and the touched-path sets are equal.
   **Do NOT use `git patch-id`** — it strips whitespace, so 8-space and 2-space Python indentation hash identically (verified 2026-08-05; see #21). It would carry a `Sound` verdict onto semantically changed code.
2. **No base overlap.** `git diff --name-only <reviewed-base>..<new-base>` ∩ the branch's touched paths is empty.
3. **Clean integration.** `git merge-tree --write-tree` against current base → single tree, exit 0.
4. **Provenance.** The carried-from marker is `Sound`, `critical: 0`, and belongs to this branch.

Any check failing, or any input unavailable, falls through to an ordinary full re-review. The failure direction is always "review it properly."

## Marker provenance

The marker records `"carriedFrom": "<reviewed head>"` and `"carryProof": "<checks passed>"`. Provenance for humans and telemetry only — `evaluateMarker` never reads them, so a forged value authorizes nothing the ordinary rules would not.

**Coordinate with cowrite#1068** (version the review-marker contract as a committed schema doc + drift guard) — it owns `conflict:review-marker-contract` and these fields must land in its schema.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `evaluateMarker` and both gates untouched (assert by diff).
- [ ] The four checks live in **one** function with property tests — the erosion concern in #21 is answered by keeping the condition in a single tested place, not scattered.
- [ ] Property test: a whitespace-only change to a touched path **refuses** the carry (the patch-id trap, pinned as a regression).
- [ ] Property test: a commit dropped during rebase refuses the carry.
- [ ] Carry only when all four pass; every other path is a full re-review.
- [ ] Chained carries permitted only when the chain root is a real full review, and check 2 runs against the **root's** base — not the immediate predecessor's — so successive clean rebases cannot drift from what was reviewed.
- [ ] `Needs Minor Revision` / `Requires Significant Correction` never carries (check 4).
- [ ] Carried rounds emit a distinguishable `review_round` so both the saving and any disagreement are measurable.
- [ ] Regression fixtures replay real histories — cowrite#1079's rebase **carries**; cowrite#1157's round-6 doc correction **does not** (content changed → ordinary re-review).
- [ ] `npm run test:harness` green.

## Conflict domains

`conflict:review-marker-contract`, `conflict:harness-run-loop` (text — no Rigger label vocabulary yet).

**Execution kind:** change · **Tier:** Opus · **High-Risk:** Yes

**What changed from the filed text.** Rules 1 and 5 no longer call operations through sample calls.
Five findings in a row (R3-B1, R4-B1, R5-B1, R6-B1, and C1 and C2 on PR #246) showed that a rule
which infers what an operation does from one chosen call leaks. The rules now hold Delta G (#247)
by what a module imports. They follow the architect's ruling on the #214 redesign, archived on #211:

- **Bindings, not reachability (R214-B2).** A rule fails on a module that imports a binding which
  resolves, through re-exports, to a function defined in a side the module's directory may not
  reach. It does not fail on what a module reaches through other layers' functions. L3 calling L2,
  which writes, and the CLI calling L3's claim-only call are the ruled structure.
- **Permitted importers.**
  - `src/scheduling/` imports the read side only.
  - `src/workflow/` alone imports the item-write side.
  - `src/cli/` alone imports the schema-write side.
  - Any directory may import the read side.

  such as `setField(item, field, value)`, stays a review finding.
- **No whole-file exemption (R214-B4).** `doctor.mjs` and `init.mjs` may spawn processes, because
  they probe local tools. No module outside the runners may name `gh`, so the exception's property
  is checked, not cited.

L3, which reads N itself (ruling 5, §4).

- **Rule 6.** The test fails when any module outside `src/cli/` and the schema-write side imports a binding that resolves, through re-exports, to a function defined in the schema-write side.
- **Re-exports.** The test fails when a module under `src/workflow/` re-exports a binding that resolves to a function defined in the item-write side, or a module under `src/cli/` re-exports one that resolves to a function defined in the schema-write side.
- **Rule 2.** The test fails when any module under `src/scheduling/` references `kinds`, a card's labels or a card's body.
- **Rule 3.** The test fails when any module under `src/scheduling/` reads `board.priority` from the config.
- **Rule 4.** The test fails when any module under `src/cli/` references `concurrency`.
- **Rule 7, first half.** The test fails when any module under `src/` imports `node:child_process`, other than the forge adapter's runner modules, `src/cli/doctor.mjs` and `src/cli/init.mjs`.
- **Rule 7, second half.** The test fails when any module under `src/` other than the runner modules holds `gh` as a string literal in code, whether in single quotes, double quotes or backticks. Comments do not count.
- The pull request lists every command `src/cli/doctor.mjs` and `src/cli/init.mjs` spawn at its head, and none is `gh`. At `88c61d3` they spawned `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `gh auth status` and `claude auth status --json` (`doctor`), and `git remote get-url origin` (`init`). #216 (M1-03) moves `gh auth status` onto the read runner.
- **Dynamic imports.** The test fails, naming the file, on any dynamic `import()` whose specifier it cannot resolve to a file under `src/`. The one exception is `doctor.mjs`'s load of the consumer's config file, and the pull request shows that it is the only exempt case at the head.

This card builds Delta G's three sides (#247). The architect's ruling on the #214 redesign, archived
on #211, sets the terms:

- **Admission.** Each side's runner refuses any request outside its side, and admits one operation
  per request, from an explicit allowlist.

content.title: M1-04 — L2's acceptance form check
content.body:
Part of **M1**, `docs/v0-build-plan.md` §4 M1. **Author:** the PM, as the decomposing role (`D18` rule 4; `D20`). Filed by the M1 coordinator on 2026-09-24 at the owner's instruction, without taking authorship (`D20` rule 2).

Citations in the form `ruling N`, `R#-B#`, `r#-N#` and `§N` point to the architect's rulings, the reviewer's verdicts and the draft's sections. All of them are archived on #211. Card references are written as issue numbers, with the draft id beside each.

---

- **Depends on:** delta A on `main`.
- **Lands in:** L2 `src/workflow/`.
- **Real board:** no.
- **Self-hosting paths:** none.

**Why.** E2's admission half, and `R-CARD-7` and `R-CARD-8`.

**The form is defined on the body's source text, not on how GitHub renders it.** That is the
owner's ruling D on the maker's escalation, relayed by the coordinator on 2026-09-24. The
escalation is issue comment 5826898521 on this card. The check parses no Markdown beyond the lines
below, and calls no renderer.

**The rule.** A line's indentation is the run of space characters at its start.

- **Fences.** A fence opens at a line indented zero to three spaces that begins with three or more
  backticks or three or more tildes. It closes at the next line indented zero to three spaces that
  holds only a run of at least as many of the same character. A fence left unclosed runs to the end
  of the body. Every line from an opening fence to its closing fence is inside the fence, and the
  rest of the rule ignores it.
- **An acceptance heading.** It is an ATX heading line outside a fence: indented zero to three
  spaces, one to six `#`, then a space or the end of the line. Its text, with surrounding whitespace
  and any closing run of `#` removed, is exactly `Acceptance`, case-sensitive.
- **The section.** It runs from that heading to the next ATX heading line outside a fence with the
  same number of `#` or fewer, or to the end of the body. A deeper heading does not end it, and
  neither does anything that is not an ATX heading line.
- **A plain bullet.** It is a line in the section, outside a fence, indented zero to three spaces,
  that begins with `-`, `*` or `+` followed by a space. The item's text is the rest of that line
  after the marker and that space. A line whose indentation holds a tab is not a plain bullet.
- **What does not count.** A bullet whose text begins `[ ]` or `[x]`, in either case, is a task-list
  item. A bullet whose text is empty or only whitespace is no item. Neither counts.
- **The acceptance.** It is every plain bullet in every such section. Lines that follow a bullet
  and are not bullets belong to no item.

**How that settles each case the maker listed** on this card (comment 5826898521). Each case is an
item below.

- A bullet in a blockquote (`> - …`) begins with `>`, so it is not a plain bullet.
- A heading in a blockquote or a list item (`> ## Acceptance`, `- ## Acceptance`) is not an ATX
  heading line.
- A bullet inside `<details>` is a plain bullet. HTML is not modelled.
- `## **Acceptance**` has the text `**Acceptance**`, so it is not an acceptance heading.
- A setext heading is not an ATX heading line. It neither opens a section nor ends one.
- An item with a link is compared on its source text, URL included.
- `- <!-- fill in -->` has non-empty source text, so it is an item.
- The maker's round-1 cases:
  - A: a bullet indented four spaces is not a plain bullet.
  - B and F: HTML does not hide or reveal a line.
  - C and D: a setext heading is not a heading here.
  - E: a nested bullet indented at most three spaces is a plain bullet.

**The restated-title rule** is the U2 ruling. An item restates the title when the two are equal
after the same normalisation of both:

- letters folded to lower case;
- runs of whitespace collapsed to one space, and trimmed;
- every Unicode punctuation character (`\p{P}`) and symbol character (`\p{S}`) deleted.

A card is refused when every item restates its title. **The punctuation step is open for the
owner:** deleting rather than spacing, and counting symbols, is the maker's implementation, kept as
it stands. `R-CARD-8` makes these two refusals the whole check, so the falsifier ranges over what L2
returns.

## Acceptance

- Given a card whose body holds no acceptance heading outside a fence, the form check refuses it. The test declares `R-CARD-7`.
- Given a card with no acceptance, the refusal names the card's number and gives missing acceptance as the reason. The test declares `R-CARD-7`.
- Given a card whose acceptance section holds no plain bullet, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose section's only bullets are task-list items (`- [ ]` or `- [x]`), the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose bullets sit under `Acceptance criteria` and under no acceptance heading, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose only heading is `## acceptance`, in lower case, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose only heading is `## **Acceptance**`, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given three cards whose acceptance headings are at levels `#`, `##` and `###`, each holding one plain bullet that does not restate the title, the form check admits all three.
- Given a card whose heading is `## Acceptance ##`, holding one plain bullet that does not restate the title, the form check admits it.
- Given a card whose `## Acceptance` section holds one bullet that does not restate the title, followed by a `##` heading holding bullets that do, the form check admits it.
- Given a card whose `## Acceptance` section holds bullets that restate the title, then a `### Notes` heading with one bullet that does not, the form check admits it.
- Given a card whose section's only bullet is indented four spaces, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose section's only bullet is indented by a tab, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose section's only bullet is indented two spaces, as a nested bullet, and does not restate the title, the form check admits it.
- Given a card whose only acceptance heading and bullet sit inside a backtick fence, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose only acceptance heading and bullet sit inside a tilde fence, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose section opens a fence that is never closed, followed by a bullet that does not restate the title, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose `## Acceptance` section's only bullet is `> - ` followed by text that does not restate the title, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose only heading is `> ## Acceptance`, followed by `> - ` and text that does not restate the title, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose only heading is `- ## Acceptance`, followed by `  - ` and text that does not restate the title, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose `## Acceptance` section holds `<details>`, a blank line, a bullet that does not restate the title, a blank line and `</details>`, the form check admits it.
- Given a card whose only heading is a setext heading, `Acceptance` underlined with `---`, followed by a bullet that does not restate the title, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose `## Acceptance` section holds a setext heading `Notes` underlined with `===`, followed by a bullet that does not restate the title, the form check admits it.
- Given a card whose section's only bullet is `-` followed only by spaces, the form check refuses it, with missing acceptance as the reason.
- Given a card whose section's only bullet is `- <!-- fill in -->`, the form check admits it.
- Given the title `Add a verb` and the only item `[Add a verb](https://example.com)`, the form check admits the card, because the item's source text holds the URL.
- Given two acceptance headings in one body, where only the second section holds a bullet that does not restate the title, the form check admits the card.
- Given a card whose every acceptance item matches its title after normalising, the form check refuses it. The test declares `R-CARD-8`.
- Given a card whose acceptance only restates its title, the refusal names the card's number and gives a restated title as the reason. The test declares `R-CARD-8`.
- Given the title `Support C++` and the only item `Support C`, the form check refuses the card as a restated title. That follows the open punctuation step.
- Given a card with one item that restates the title and one that does not, the form check admits it.
- Given any card whose section holds at least one plain bullet that does not restate its title, the form check does not refuse it. A test covers at least CRLF line endings, the `*` and `+` markers, an HTML comment inside the section, trailing spaces after the heading, and an empty title. The test declares `R-CARD-8`.
- Every refusal the form check returns anywhere in this card's tests carries one of exactly two reasons, checked by a test that collects every refusal result.
- A reviewer reading the diff finds that every code path returning a refusal returns one of those two reasons.
- The form check reads only the body's source text. A reviewer reading the diff finds no Markdown renderer or parser dependency and no network call, and `package.json`'s `dependencies` are unchanged.
- The body of issue #182, as `gh issue view 182` returned it on a date the test names, passes the form check.
- After this card's tests land, `npm run matrix:check` exits 0, and the rows for `R-CARD-7` and `R-CARD-8` each name at least one test.

Part of **M1**, `docs/v0-build-plan.md` §4 M1. **Author:** the PM, as the decomposing role (`D18` rule 4; `D20`). Filed by the M1 coordinator on 2026-09-24 at the owner's instruction, without taking authorship (`D20` rule 2).

Citations in the form `ruling N`, `R#-B#`, `r#-N#` and `§N` point to the architect's rulings, the reviewer's verdicts and the draft's sections. All of them are archived on #211. Card references are written as issue numbers, with the draft id beside each.

---

- **Depends on:**
  - #225 (M1-06)'s merged verb.
  - #235 (M1-21)'s board 6 run, after which `Owner` is an option on board 6.
  - The filed M1 cards added to board 6.
  - The owner's approval of the staging.
  - A quiet window: every card of waves 0–6 merged, and no card of wave 8 or later started, so that no M1
    card sits in Coding or Review, and at least three unstarted M1 cards remain to stage (review
    r4-N3; §4).
- **Lands in:** no production code. Staging is done by hand, never by code (G3).
- **Real board:** reads board 6, and **stages cards on it**. It moves the named cards to Ready, sets
  their Priority, and restores them afterwards.
- **Self-hosting paths:** none.

**Why.** E4, as the plan states it: the printed order is exactly the declared priority order, with
ties broken by issue number. It must also differ from four orders that ignore priority: issue number
ascending, issue number descending, column position, and column position reversed.

- That needs at least three cards, because with two cards the two issue-number orders already cover
  every ordering.
- I don't know whether `gh`'s item order follows status changes or project position (review r3-N2).
  So the cards are moved first, their positions are read, and only then are the Priority values
  chosen. The values are chosen so that the expected order differs from all four orders as read.
- A redo would head the printed order ahead of the staged cards, and E4 says "exactly". So the run
  requires that no unclaimed Coding or Review card is on board 6 (review r3-N3).
- Every staging write is announced before it is made, and undone afterwards (review B3(b), r2-N5,
  r2-N6).

## Acceptance

- Before any write to board 6, the maker comments on this card naming every command it will run there. The comment lists the cards to stage: open M1 cards on board 6 that are in Backlog with no branch and no pull request, excluding this card. It gives each card's current column and Priority value, as `gh` read them.
- That comment lists at least three cards.
- Where fewer than three cards are eligible, no write is made to board 6, and the card is escalated as `ambiguous`, naming the count.
- That comment shows a `gh` read, taken when the comment was posted, in which no card is in board 6's `coding` or `review` column.
- Where that read shows any card in board 6's `coding` or `review` column, no write is made to board 6, and the card is escalated as `ambiguous`, naming those cards.
- That comment links the owner's approval of the staging.
- That comment states the sort setting of board 6's view, and says the column positions used are the order `gh` returns items in.
- After the listed cards are moved to Ready, a `gh` read shows each of them in Ready.
- After those moves, the `gh` read shows no other item on board 6 changed.
- Before any Priority value is set, a second comment gives the staged cards' positions as that read returned them, and the value each will receive. It writes out the four naive orders (issue number ascending, issue number descending, position, and position reversed), and the expected pull order, which differs from each of them.
- After the values are set, a `gh` read shows each staged card with its announced value, and no other item on board 6 changed.
- The pull request includes the full output of `rigger plan` against this repository and board 6, from an engine installed from a tarball `npm pack` produced at a `main` SHA the pull request names, installed outside the checkout.
- That run's working directory was a fresh clone from `https://github.com/williacj/rigger.git`.
- The pull order `rigger plan` printed equals the expected order posted in the second comment.
- The printed order differs from each of the four naive orders, and the pull request writes all four out.
- After the run, each staged card whose column and Priority value are unchanged since staging is restored to its prior column and value, shown by a `gh` read.
- Any staged card whose column or value someone else changed after staging is left as it is, and named in the pull request.
- `rigger plan` is the only Rigger verb this card runs against board 6.

content.body:
